title: Curated alert decomposition and SLO-aware suppressor playbook
creator: Sara Nguyen
description: Noise from multi-region failover and transient throttles is generating high page volume and on-call fatigue. This ticket defines and implements a layered alert decomposition and SLO-aware suppression mechanism plus curated on-call runbooks that allow safe automated mitigation (circuit-breaker triggers and load-shedding recipes) while preserving critical customer-visible SLO signals.
background: Over the last 6 months our paging volume doubled during cross-region capacity shifts. Pager fatigue correlates with longer MTTD for high-impact incidents. Existing alert rules are flat thresholds per metric and do not account for deployment-level context (region, capacity tier, rollback events) or SLO weight. We need an approach that decomposes noisy aggregated alerts into orthogonal signals, suppresses non-actionable noise, and enables automated, reversible mitigations tied to runbook steps.
proposal: 1) Implement a hierarchical suppressor that evaluates alerts with SLO-weight and region-impact factors. 2) Decompose aggregated alerts into root-cause intents (eg. capacity-pressure, kernel OOMs, degraded-kv-cache) using a deterministic rule set and light ML classifier for pattern matching. 3) Wire suppressor decisions into the runbook automation engine: low-severity noisy alerts get deduplicated and delayed; medium-severity alerts can trigger automated, reversible circuit-breaker (traffic steering to secondary region) steps after cross-checks; high-severity alerts still page immediately. 4) Deliver curated runbook templates with explicit rollback criteria, safety gates, and playbook telemetry for post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Suppressor reduces duplicate pages by >=50% during simulated multi-region failover (synthetic test).
No-page-delay policy for high-impact SLO breaches (latency P99 > SLO) remains unchanged.
Automated circuit-breaker action can be toggled per-customer and has an audit log for every decision.
Runbook templates published in Confluence and linked from alert notifications.
Post-deploy chaos test: trigger region-induced capacity constraint; suppression must prevented non-actionable pages while ensuring two highest-severity incidents still page.
tasks: Design suppressor scoring: create scoring factors (metric severity, SLO-weight, region-impact, recent-mitigation-history).
Implement rule-based decomposition for common intents (capacity, cache-eviction, infra-oom, routing-imbalance).
Prototype light-weight classifier for pattern matching (serverless inference, logs + metrics fingerprint).
Extend alerting pipeline: insert suppressor step before pager and attach decision metadata to alert payload.
Create canary runbook templates with automated circuit-breaker and load-shed steps (including safety checks and rollback triggers).
Integrate audit logging (immutable events) and update Console incident UI to show suppressor decisions.
Write e2e chaos tests and synthetic traffic generator for failover simulations.
Run internal on-call drill and collect feedback; iterate on suppressor thresholds.
risks: Over-suppression could hide real SLO breaches — mitigated by explicit high-severity bypass and periodic audit queries.
Classifier false positives in early model could mislabel intents — keep rule-based fallback and conservative default behavior.
Automated circuit-breakers may interact poorly with customer routing policies — require opt-in per customer and feature flags.
Operational complexity increase in alerting pipeline — include observability and debug endpoints, plus runbook for debugging suppressor decisions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged internal rollout for staging and internal prod (1 week). 2) Enable for non-critical customer tenants with monitoring (2 weeks). 3) Run chaos test and on-call drills; collect metrics. 4) Gradual opt-in for customers and update docs. Each step gated by acceptance criteria and SRE sign-off.
test_plan: - Unit tests for scoring logic and decomposition rules. - Integration tests for alert pipeline insertion. - Synthetic multi-region failover scenario that asserts page reduction and SLO signal preservation. - On-call drill script to validate runbook automation and human override flows.
observability: Add metrics: suppressor_decisions_total{decision=dedupe|delay|page|auto_mitigate}, suppressor_latency_ms, classifier_confidence, auto_mitigations_executed_total. Expose decision traces linked to alert ids in Console incidents view.
documentation: Confluence: /reliability/alert-suppressor-playbooks (draft). Links to templates and runbook examples will be added. Update on-call handbook with new escalation windows and override commands.
